recommendations: Consider tightening SR1 to also require num_consumers to be exact (==2) rather than '>= len(direct_consumers)' to avoid rewarding a report that pads extra bogus consumers per bit while still meeting the >= threshold.

The false-positive threshold in SR4 (0.15) permits some slack; consider documenting this threshold in participant-facing evaluation/README.md so expectations around precision are clearer without revealing the exact ground-truth suspect set.

requirement_results.evidence: evaluate.py validates presence and types of all 5 top-level fields; baseline (valid JSON) passes FR1.
evaluate.py checks exactly 8 fanout_map entries, key_bit 0-7 coverage, and num_consumers==len(consumer_instances); baseline passes since it has 8 well-formed entries.
evaluate.py verifies all instance names in fanout_map/suspect_instances exist in inputs/netlist.v; baseline only references real instances so passes.
evaluate.py checks verdict in {trojan_present, trojan_absent}; baseline uses trojan_absent, a valid enum value, so FR4 passes even though SR3 fails.

evaluate.py structurally traces netlist.v to derive direct consumers per bit (u_round_xor<i>, u_shadow_ff<i>) and fails baseline (num_consumers=1, missing shadow_ff) as shown in differential vulnerable_run output; golden reference with 2 consumers per bit passes.
evaluate.py computes ground-truth suspect set via transitive fanout trace and requires recall==1.0; baseline's empty suspect_instances fails SR2 as confirmed in vulnerable_run log.
String equality check against 'trojan_present'; baseline's 'trojan_absent' fails as shown in vulnerable_run output.
False-positive rate computed only over valid, non-empty suspect_instances; baseline's empty list explicitly fails SR4 ('suspect_instances is empty...'), and golden passes with 0% FP rate.
Differential harness confirms vulnerable/baseline run exits 1 with FR1-FR4 pass but SR1-SR4 fail, matching acceptance criteria that naive baseline fails SR1-SR3 (and SR4).
Golden run exits 0 with all 8 checks passing, matching the private reference_solution.json structure (verdict=trojan_present, 2-consumer fanout_map, 9-instance suspect set).

README.md, metadata.json, design_brief.md, and cell_library.v contain no mention of trojan, shadow registers, exfil, CWE ids, or SR ids; framed as plain fanout-verification engineering task. Evaluation README also avoids spoilers, only stating that structural ground truth is checked.

Metadata declares detection_rate, false_positive_rate, fanout_accuracy, verdict_correctness, inference_latency; evaluate.py's SR1/SR2/SR3/SR4 checks directly operationalize fanout_accuracy, detection_rate, verdict_correctness, and false_positive_rate respectively, and wall-clock timing is measurable by harness around evaluate.py execution.

requirement_map lists FR1-FR4 (functional) and SR1-SR4 (security) each mapped to evaluate.py with distinct detection logic; mutation_score 1.0 and per_requirement coverage/discrimination all true confirm each check is active and discriminating.
